# Company 009 — Document-to-Workflow Engine

**Company ID:** `company:future:009`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:009`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-009-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only.

## Business identity

Purpose: turn unstructured/semi-structured documents and attachments into verified structured data and downstream business workflows.

Problem: invoices, applications, contracts, claims, forms, scans, receipts and emailed documents create manual reading/data-entry/routing work; extraction-only tools stop before validation, reconciliation and action.

Value: document intake through extraction, validation, business rules, human exceptions, workflow execution and evidence.

Delivery: API, SaaS inbox/workspace, embedded SDK, batch ingestion, email/SFTP connectors, private runner, vertical document packs.

## Product tree

- Universal Document Intake — PDF/image/scan/Office/spreadsheet/email attachment/form.
- OCR/Layout Understanding — pages, tables, handwriting where viable, signatures/marks detection.
- Document Classification — type/subtype/source/priority/sensitivity.
- Structured Extraction — fields/tables/entities/clauses/line items.
- Validation Engine — schema, ranges, reference data, cross-field rules.
- Reconciliation Engine — compare PO/invoice, application/records, claim/policy, form/master data.
- Document Routing — queues, owners, systems, approvals.
- Exception Workspace — low-confidence/conflict/missing data/human correction.
- Document Generation — validated output forms, letters, reports, summaries.
- Form/Template Studio — schemas, extraction packs, rules, examples.
- Contract/Clause Pack; Invoice/AP Pack; Claims Pack; Application/Onboarding Pack; Receipt/Expense Pack; Compliance Evidence Pack; Logistics/Shipping Pack.
- Continuous Document Workflow — monitor inbound folders/email and trigger repeatable processes.
- API/SDK/OEM/Private Deployment.

## Feature/customer/vertical trees

Features: OCR, layout/table, rotation/quality, language, classification, field confidence, source bounding boxes, validation, reference lookup, duplicate detection, version comparison, signatures/checkboxes, redaction, document splitting/merging, attachment threading, human review, audit, retention, export, workflow builder, webhooks/API, batch, accessibility/localization.

Customers: finance/AP/AR, insurance/claims, legal/admin, healthcare admin, HR, procurement, government, logistics, property/construction, education/nonprofit, SaaS platforms, BPO/outsourcing, developers.

Verticals: accounts payable, insurance, credentialing, onboarding, lending/admin only with appropriate regulation, logistics/BOL/POD, construction submittals/COIs, legal contract intake, healthcare administrative forms, public applications, grant administration, ecommerce returns/warranty.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain understands document type, semantic fields/clauses, workflow context, ambiguous text and exception reason. It can recommend mappings/rules, summarize, classify, detect likely inconsistencies. Deterministic schemas/rules/reconciliation own acceptance and protected downstream actions. Confidence must be explicit; low confidence escalates.

Architecture: OCR/CV/layout models, deterministic parser/schema validators, relational master/reference data, LLM/vision model for semantic extraction where needed, model routing, rules engine, entity resolution, workflow/state engine, object store, provenance/coordinate refs, human review queue.

## Agent tree

Intake Classifier, Extraction Agent, Table/Line-Item Agent, Clause Analyst, Validation Agent, Reconciliation Agent, Duplicate/Fraud Signal Agent, Routing Agent, Human-Review Coordinator, Template/Schema Agent, Privacy/Redaction Agent, Document Generation Agent, Integration Agent, QA Agent.

## Deterministic services

File ingestion/virus scan; MIME parser; OCR/layout; image preprocessing; schema registry; field validators; reference-data lookup; duplicate/hash service; reconciliation rules; confidence thresholds; object storage; retention; queue; workflow engine; human review state; export/webhook; audit.

## Inputs / outputs / workflows

Inputs: files/scans/images/email attachments, document schemas/templates, reference/master data, workflow rules, customer corrections.

Outputs: structured JSON/tables, validated records, routed tasks, downstream API calls, generated docs, exceptions, evidence.

Workflow: ingest → malware/type/quality scan → classify/split → OCR/layout/semantic extract → confidence/provenance → validate/reference → reconcile → exception/human review → approve structured record → trigger authorized workflow → verify downstream result → retain/delete/evidence.

## Integrations / API

Email, cloud drives, SFTP, scanners/mobile capture, accounting/ERP, CRM, claims/policy systems, HRIS, procurement, DMS, e-sign, databases/warehouses, workflow engines, ticketing, object storage. APIs for upload/job/status/result/schema/template/validation/review/webhook/export.

## Data / moat

Document templates/schemas, labeled examples, extraction corrections, field-coordinate provenance, validation/reconciliation rules, document-type ontology, confidence/calibration and vertical exception corpus. Customer documents remain isolated; training reuse opt-in only.

## Monetization / distribution

Per page/document/field/job, vertical pack, seats/reviewers, API, private deployment, dedicated models, enterprise retention/compliance, OEM, managed review. Distribution via accounting/insurance/HR/procurement/DMS partners, developer APIs, vertical integrators and marketplaces.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Documents may hold PII/financial/health/legal data. Virus/malware scan, encryption, least privilege, regional/private processing, redaction, short retention, no-training default, review access controls, audit, deletion/export, customer-specific keys optional, protected downstream actions.

## Failure / edge cases

Poor scan, handwriting, mixed languages, nested tables, wrong document type, duplicate/resubmitted doc, forged/altered content, prompt injection in document text, OCR hallucination, conflicting reference data, partial page, password/encrypted file, huge file, hidden attachments. Treat document content as untrusted data, not instructions; use confidence/provenance and deterministic validation.

## Scale / moat / platform

Micro: thousands docs/month. ~$100K ARR: vertical templates/review tooling. ~$1M: enterprise/private/custom packs. ~$10M: large multi-vertical processing and partner ecosystem. ~$100M+: document intelligence/workflow infrastructure with broad OEM/API use.

Overlap #8 general workflow, #31 business forms, #35 claims, #48 AP verification, #52 COI, #64 inbox. Company 009 stays document-centric extraction→validated workflow.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** untrusted-content boundary, artifact/provenance refs, confidence/verification contracts, workflow/action gates, storage/retention interfaces.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center should treat documents as untrusted inputs and preserve provenance; generic artifact/workflow contracts after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** company isolation/private processing seams, model routing, review/evaluation interfaces.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** extraction packs/models/vertical connectors/UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** dedicated OCR/model fleets, broad marketplace.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. **Complete Product Tree:** intake/OCR/classification/extraction/validation/reconciliation/routing/review/generation/template studio/vertical packs/API/private/OEM.
2. **Complete Feature Tree:** file handling, layout/table/language/confidence/provenance/rules/duplicates/version/redaction/review/audit/retention/workflow/API.
3. **Complete Customer Tree:** finance, insurance, legal/admin, health admin, HR, procurement, government, logistics, construction, education, SaaS/BPO/devs.
4. **Complete Vertical Tree:** AP, claims, credentialing, onboarding, logistics, COI, contracts, health forms, public/grant, returns/warranty.
5. **Complete Brain Capability Tree:** semantic extraction/classification/mapping/explanation; deterministic verification/action.
6. **Complete Agent Tree:** classifier/extractor/table/clause/validation/reconcile/duplicate/routing/review/template/privacy/generation/integration/QA.
7. **Complete Service Tree:** ingest/scan/OCR/schema/validation/reference/hash/reconcile/confidence/storage/retention/queue/workflow/review/export/audit.
8. **Complete Workflow Tree:** ingest→untrusted scan→extract→verify→review→structured record→authorized workflow→verification.
9. **Complete Integration Tree:** email/files/SFTP/mobile/accounting/ERP/CRM/claims/HR/procurement/DMS/e-sign/data/workflow/tickets.
10. **Complete Data Tree:** files, schemas, labels, corrections, provenance, reference, rules, exceptions, results.
11. **Complete API/Developer Tree:** upload/job/status/result/schema/template/validation/review/webhooks/export.
12. **Complete Monetization Tree:** pages/docs/fields/jobs/packs/seats/API/private/dedicated/retention/OEM/managed review.
13. **Complete Distribution Tree:** vertical integrations, marketplaces, developer/partner channels.
14. **Complete Automation Tree:** intake/classify/extract/validate/reconcile/route/generate; low confidence escalates.
15. **Complete Moat Tree:** template/correction corpus, calibration, vertical rules, integrations, reliable provenance.
16. **Complete Platform Tree:** extraction → validated document operations → vertical workflow platform.
17. **Complete Risk Tree:** sensitive docs, malicious content, OCR errors, forged docs, overretention, wrong action.
18. **Complete Scale Tree:** small queues → vertical enterprise → large multi-region/OEM.
19. **Complete Spinoff Tree:** existing #31/#35/#48/#52/#64 cover specialist products.
20. **Command Center Dependencies:** artifact/provenance, security, model routing, workflow/Agency, retention, company isolation.
21. **Design-Now Requirements:** untrusted content + confidence/provenance + deterministic action verification.
22. **Build-Now Requirements:** shared artifact/input-security contracts after reverse-map.
23. **Safe-to-Defer Requirements:** specific OCR/models/templates/connectors/review portal/pricing.
24. **Autonomous Mature State:** intake/extraction/validation/routing operate automatically; exceptions route to humans; James sees strategic/protected decisions only.

## Saturation result

Further document niches become vertical packs or existing specialist portfolio companies; no additional top-level company is needed.

# Company 010 — Subscription Revenue Recovery Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:010`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:010`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-010-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no payment collection, customer communication or retention offer execution.

## Business identity

Purpose: recover otherwise-lost recurring revenue by detecting payment risk, coordinating compliant retries/dunning, reducing involuntary churn, identifying voluntary churn risk, and measuring verified recovered value.

Problem: recurring businesses lose revenue to failed payments, stale cards, poor retry timing, confusing communications, unnecessary cancellations and weak win-back workflows.

Value: deterministic payment-state orchestration plus predictive/behavioral assistance, with customer-respectful controls and clear recovery attribution.

Delivery: SaaS, billing-provider apps, API/SDK, managed recovery workflows, enterprise/private data mode, embedded/OEM retention modules.

## Product tree

- Payment Failure Monitor.
- Smart Retry Scheduler — provider/rule/issuer response-aware, bounded and compliant.
- Dunning Communications Orchestrator — email/SMS/in-app with consent/channel rules; execution protected.
- Payment Method Update Portal / hosted link integration.
- Involuntary Churn Prevention.
- Voluntary Churn Risk Signals — usage/engagement/support/plan context.
- Cancellation Save Flow — reason capture, pause/downgrade/options; no dark patterns.
- Retention Offer Engine — policy constrained, profitability/fairness-aware.
- Win-Back Campaign Planner — consent-aware, not spam.
- Revenue Recovery Analytics — recovered/at-risk/lost attribution.
- Segment/Benchmark Analytics — privacy-safe.
- Subscription Health API.
- Recovery Experimentation — retry/message/offer tests with guardrails.
- SaaS, memberships, media/subscription commerce vertical packs.
- Enterprise Multi-Brand/Entity Console.
- White-label/OEM recovery engine.

## Feature/customer/vertical trees

Features: payment event normalization, decline taxonomy, retry windows, card/account update status, grace periods, account state, contact consent, message templates, throttles, time zones, plan/value/margin, churn reason, usage health, experiment assignment, holdouts, customer journey, recovery attribution, refund/chargeback awareness, audit, approval, data export/delete.

Customers: SaaS, subscription ecommerce, media/membership, marketplaces with recurring fees, apps, service subscriptions, education/communities, enterprise recurring-revenue products.

Verticals: B2B SaaS, B2C apps, memberships, creator/community subscriptions, subscription boxes, media/content, recurring professional services. Highly regulated payments/credit/insurance require specialized constraints and may be unsuitable without compliance review.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain knows account/subscription/payment/engagement/support context within allowed scope. It reasons about failure type and retention likelihood, predicts churn/recovery probability, optimizes retry/message/offer within hard limits, recommends save/win-back actions, monitors outcomes. It cannot move money, change contracts, send communications or grant discounts outside deterministic policy/authorization.

Architecture: payment event state machine, retry rules, subscription ledger, consent/notification engine, experimentation/causal analysis, churn models, time-series features, LLM for message draft/explanation/support signal extraction only, policy engine for offers/contact frequency/fairness.

## Agent tree

Payment Failure Analyst, Retry Optimizer, Dunning Planner, Churn Analyst, Retention Offer Analyst, Win-Back Planner, Experiment Agent, Customer Experience/Policy Agent, Revenue Attribution Agent, Integration Health Agent, Support Signal Agent, Privacy/Consent Agent, Finance Reconciliation Agent.

## Deterministic services

Payment webhook normalization; idempotent event ledger; retry scheduler; billing-provider connectors; entitlement/subscription state; consent/preferences; communication queue; offer/policy rules; experiment assignment; attribution engine; payment method update link/session; audit; rate/contact limiter; reconciliation.

## Inputs / outputs / workflows

Inputs: billing/payment events, subscription state, account value/margin, consent, usage/engagement, support signals, plan/contracts, owner policies.

Outputs: retry schedules, recommended messages/offers, account tasks, risk scores, recovered-revenue evidence, churn/retention analytics.

Involuntary workflow: failure event → classify → customer/account state → retry policy → retry/notification authorization → execute through billing/comms provider → verify state → recover/grace/cancel/escalate → attribution.

Voluntary workflow: risk → evidence/features → recommendation → permitted intervention/offer → customer choice → verify retention/churn → experiment attribution.

## Integrations / API

Stripe-like billing/payment providers, subscription platforms, app stores where data accessible, CRM, support, product analytics, email/SMS/in-app notification, accounting/BI, entitlement systems, data warehouses. # Company 011 — Automated Benchmarking Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:011`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:011`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-011-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only.

## Business identity

Purpose: produce trustworthy peer benchmarks across financial, operational, sales, marketing, support, product, engineering, AI, HR and industry metrics while protecting customer confidentiality.

Problem: companies lack context for KPIs; public averages are stale, incomparable or poorly segmented; internal teams waste time collecting peer data and normalizing definitions.

Value: normalized benchmark definitions, cohorting, confidence, trend, peer recommendations and proprietary indices.

Delivery: SaaS dashboards, benchmark reports, API, embedded analytics, industry packs, private peer groups, white-label/OEM benchmark modules.

## Product tree

- Financial Benchmarks — revenue growth, margins, spend mix, runway/cash efficiency, unit economics where comparable.
- Operational Benchmarks — cycle time, throughput, utilization, quality, service levels.
- Sales/RevOps Benchmarks — pipeline, conversion, velocity, retention/expansion.
- Marketing Benchmarks — channel efficiency, conversion, CAC-related measures where definitions align.
- Support Benchmarks — volume, resolution, repeat contact, satisfaction, QA.
- Product Benchmarks — activation, engagement, retention, feature adoption.
- Engineering Benchmarks — delivery, reliability, incident/change metrics.
- AI Benchmarks — model/agent quality/cost/latency/reliability/ROI.
- HR/People Benchmarks — hiring/retention/training metrics with privacy controls.
- Industry/Geographic/Size Cohorts.
- Proprietary Indices and composite scores.
- Peer Recommendation Engine.
- Benchmark API/Embedded BI.
- Executive Benchmark Reports.
- Private Consortium/Peer Group Benchmarking.
- Data Definition Registry and Metric Translation Service.
- Benchmark Experiment/Scenario Tools.

## Feature/customer/vertical trees

Features: metric definitions, mappings, cohort filters, minimum cohort size, anonymization, winsorization/outlier policy, time periods, currency/unit normalization, confidence intervals, percentile bands, trend, peer selection, data-quality scores, source provenance, private cohorts, export/API, alerts, comparisons, scenario targets, role access, accessible/localized dashboards.

Customers: SMB/midmarket/enterprise leaders, finance/ops/revops/product/engineering/support/AI teams, consultants, PE/VC operating teams where lawful, associations, franchises, multi-location businesses, SaaS platforms embedding benchmarks.

Verticals: SaaS, ecommerce/retail, agencies/services, field service, construction/home services, logistics, support centers, software/AI, healthcare admin, nonprofit, education, franchise/multi-location. Vertical packs must standardize definitions before comparison.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain understands metric semantics, cohort comparability, missingness, confounders and distribution. It reasons about whether a benchmark is meaningful, identifies drivers and recommends realistic improvement ranges. It must not invent peer data or reveal identifiable competitors.

Architecture: deterministic metric registry/normalization, privacy thresholding, statistical engine, time-series, cohort query layer, data warehouse, anomaly/outlier handling; LLM for mapping messy customer metric labels and explaining results, always grounded in metric definitions and aggregate evidence.

## Agent tree

Metric Ontology Agent, Data Mapping Agent, Cohort Analyst, Statistical QA Agent, Privacy Threshold Agent, Benchmark Insight Agent, Industry Pack Agent, Index Designer, Data Quality Agent, Executive Report Agent, API/Integration Agent, Customer Success Diagnostics Agent.

## Deterministic services

Metric schema registry; ingest/ETL; normalization; identity/tenant isolation; anonymization/aggregation; minimum cohort enforcement; statistical percentile/confidence engine; cohort query; time-series; index calculator; data-quality scoring; API/cache; audit; export.

## Inputs / outputs / workflows

Inputs: customer-authorized metrics, public/licensed benchmark data, metric schemas, cohort attributes, time periods, currencies/units.

Outputs: percentiles, peer bands, indices, trend, gaps, recommendations, reports, API responses.

Workflow: ingest → validate definitions → map/normalize → quality/privacy checks → assign eligible cohorts → aggregate → statistical validation → publish benchmark → monitor sample drift → revise definitions/cohorts with version evidence.

## Integrations / API

Warehouses, BI, accounting, CRM, support, analytics, HRIS, engineering/devops, AI observability, spreadsheets, data platforms. API for metric definitions, submissions, cohort eligibility, percentile/benchmark lookup, trend and index values.

## Data / moat

Metric ontology, normalization mappings, historical aggregate distributions, cohort models, industry packs, quality and comparability evidence. Moat from broad normalized coverage and trusted privacy methodology, not access to identifiable customer records.

## Monetization / distribution

Subscription by benchmark packs/seats/company size, API usage, embedded/OEM, premium historical depth, private peer groups, industry reports, enterprise custom cohorts, data licenses where permitted. Distribution via associations, consultants, SaaS/BI partners, finance/ops communities, embedded integrations.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Strict tenant isolation, minimum cohort size, disclosure controls, differential privacy where appropriate, no raw peer exposure, sensitive HR/financial metrics classified, opt-in data contribution, contractual use limits, deletion/export, regional constraints.

## Failure / edge cases

Tiny cohort, survivorship bias, definition mismatch, seasonality, bad data, outlier domination, gaming, stale cohort, currency/accounting differences, reidentification risk, selection bias. Surface confidence/sample limits and refuse misleading comparisons.

## Scale / platform

Micro: curated public/licensed datasets. ~$100K ARR: SaaS/SMB cohorts. ~$1M: multi-industry/embedded. ~$10M: large benchmark network/indices. ~$100M+: benchmark data infrastructure/standards if trust and participation compound.

Overlap #6 data subscriptions, #15 BI autopilot, #95 AI ROI. Keep #011 as normalized peer benchmarking.

**BUILD NOW:** generic metric registry/evidence hooks only after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** privacy/aggregation interface, tenant isolation, analytics/warehouse adapter seams.

**SCALE-ONLY:** large benchmark network/private consortia.

# Company 012 — AI Compliance Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:012`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:012`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-012-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; not legal/compliance advice or filing authority.

## Business identity

Purpose: continuously map controls, evidence, policies, reviews, vendor obligations and recurring compliance work against selected frameworks while preserving human/legal accountability.

Problem: compliance programs are document-heavy, repetitive, evidence-driven and difficult to keep current across systems/frameworks.

Value: evidence collection, control mapping, gap detection, recurring review, audit readiness and traceable remediation.

Delivery: SaaS, evidence API, private/VPC/self-hosted, framework packs, auditor portal, managed implementation assistance, embedded/OEM compliance module.

## Product tree

- Framework/Control Registry — SOC 2-like, ISO-like, privacy/security/internal frameworks as licensed/appropriate.
- Control Mapping Engine — many-to-many controls/evidence/policies/systems.
- Evidence Collection — APIs/files/screenshots/config snapshots/log refs, freshness.
- Policy Library & Drafting.
- Gap Analysis / Readiness Score.
- Compliance Calendar & Recurring Reviews.
- Vendor Compliance Evidence.
- Access/Permission Reviews.
- Training/Acknowledgment Tracking.
- Risk/Exception Register.
- Remediation Workflow.
- Audit Request Workspace / Auditor Portal.
- Evidence Package Export.
- Regulatory/Industry Pack adapters.
- Change Monitor integration.
- Continuous Control Monitoring.
- Compliance Analytics / Benchmarking.
- Developer API/SDK.

## Feature/customer/vertical trees

Features: control IDs/version, framework mappings, evidence requirements, source/provenance, freshness/expiry, owner, test procedure, exceptions, compensating controls, risk, remediation, review/approval, attestations, audit trail, report/export, retention/legal hold, role permissions, reminders, workflows, accessible/localized UI.

Customers: startups seeking audit readiness, SMB/midmarket, enterprise GRC/security/privacy teams, SaaS vendors, regulated-adjacent companies, MSPs/consultants, auditors as portal users, government contractors where framework scope permits.

Verticals: SaaS/cloud, ecommerce, finance operations, healthcare-adjacent admin, education, public contractors, HR platforms, data/AI vendors. Packs must not imply certification/legal interpretation.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain knows framework/control versions, evidence types, system inventory and owner policies. It reasons about mappings/gaps/duplicate evidence and recommends remediation. It may draft policies/summaries but cannot certify compliance, accept legal terms or file regulatory submissions.

Architecture: relational control/evidence graph; rules engine for freshness/coverage; document/search/RAG over licensed framework text and owner policies; event connectors; evidence hashes; LLM for mapping/drafting/explanation with citations; deterministic status calculation and approval workflow.

## Agent tree

Control Mapping Agent, Evidence Collector, Evidence Freshness Monitor, Policy Drafting Agent, Gap Analyst, Remediation Planner, Vendor Evidence Agent, Access Review Agent, Training/Acknowledgment Agent, Audit Request Coordinator, Compliance Report Agent, Framework Change Analyst, Privacy/Security Agent.

## Deterministic services

Control registry; evidence registry; connector runners; file/artifact hashing; freshness scheduler; reminder/calendar; workflow/approval; mapping graph; exception/risk store; audit ledger; export packager; retention/hold; notification service.

## Inputs / outputs / workflows

Inputs: selected frameworks, controls, policies, system/config evidence, vendor documents, training/access records, owner decisions, audit requests.

Outputs: control status, evidence map, gaps, remediation tasks, policy drafts, audit packages, recurring reviews, alerts.

Workflow: select framework → map systems/controls → define evidence/tests → collect/verify → assess freshness/coverage → identify gap → remediate/approve → continuous monitoring → audit export.

## Integrations / API

Cloud/IAM, source control/CI, ticketing, HRIS, device/endpoint/security tools, SaaS admin, data stores, vendor management, training, document storage, SIEM, identity/access review, regulation monitoring. APIs for controls/evidence/gaps/exceptions/reviews/reports.

## Data / moat

Framework/control ontology, evidence-source mappings, reusable tests, control-to-system graph, remediation history, audit-request patterns. Moat is integration/mapping depth and trustworthy evidence provenance, not private compliance evidence reuse.

## Monetization / distribution

Framework/company/entity, seats, connectors, evidence volume, enterprise/private, framework packs, auditor portal, support/implementation, OEM. Distribution via security auditors/consultants/MSPs/cloud marketplaces/dev integrations.

## Security/privacy/legal

Compliance evidence may expose system/security details. Strict tenant/company isolation, least privilege, secret redaction, immutable audit, regional/private deployment, retention, auditor time-limited access, protected policy/attestation actions. Explicitly state not legal advice/certification; licensed framework content respected.

## Failure / edge cases

Stale evidence, misleading automated pass, framework version change, unavailable connector, screenshot without provenance, compensating control nuance, false control mapping, revoked vendor cert, audit scope change, missing owner approval. Status should be `unknown/needs review` rather than fabricated compliance.

## Scale / platform

Micro: one framework. ~$100K ARR: startup/SMB readiness. ~$1M: multiple frameworks/enterprise connectors. ~$10M: continuous compliance + partner ecosystem. ~$100M+: broad governance/compliance control plane subject to regulatory/legal boundaries.

Overlap #16 regulation monitor, #24 vendor risk, #37 internal policy, #47 DSAR, #75 access review. Keep #012 as cross-framework compliance operations.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** evidence/provenance/control/version contracts, policy packs, role/approval, truth states, secret isolation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center evidence/policy/evaluation registries should support compliance-pack patterns after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** company isolation, framework pack/version interfaces, connector/evidence collector boundaries.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** actual frameworks/customer evidence/auditor portal/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large partner/auditor ecosystem and continuous global packs.
